notes.5: A minority of candidates realised that, since tRNA requires ATP to bind it to the appropriate amino acid, then mitochondria as well as rough endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi apparatus are all required in the formation of enzymes.
notes.7: Although many weaker candidates continue to find it hard to recognise α-glucose and β-glucose, the majority of candidates answered this correctly.
notes.11: Stronger candidates had no difficulty with this question, but the majority of weaker candidates incorrectly thought that the properties of glycogen were dependent on hydrogen bonds.
notes.12: Whilst almost all candidates used the information to correctly identify collagen and haemoglobin, less than a half of candidates correctly identified the antibody.
notes.14: Although the strongest candidates answered correctly, only a minority realised that the mean calculated by candidate 2 is correct as the anomalous result of ‘8’ is ignored.
notes.20: Stronger candidates had no difficulty with this question, although less able candidates were unable to link DNA uncoiling and separating with interphase.
notes.21: The majority of more able candidates were able to process this information to decide that nocodazole might work by stopping sister chromatids migrating to opposite poles.
notes.24: Whilst stronger candidates had no difficulty in converting from anticodon to codon to DNA sequence, this was challenging to the majority of weaker candidates.
notes.27: Whilst this was answered correctly by most of the more able candidates, there were many who did not fully understand the mechanics of transpiration.
notes.28: A minority of candidates thought that all three adaptations would be seen in halophytes. However, if the stomata were open most of the time the plants would lose too much water.
notes.38: Nearly two thirds of all candidates were able to use the information to determine the ecological relationships, showing good knowledge of the terminology.
notes.39: This proved straightforward for stronger candidates, who knew that only denitrifying bacteria require anaerobic soil conditions.
